start.label: The Beverly Hilton, 9876 Wilshire Blvd, Beverly Hills

homes.summary: Custom 2018 Mediterranean in the Chevy Chase foothills with canyon views, an elevator, and a private bath for every bedroom. The price was cut and it's been sitting 47 days, so there's room to talk.
highlights: Built 2018 on 0.4 acres with canyon and mountain views
Elevator between all three levels
All 4 bedrooms have their own bathroom
Big kitchen island, balcony off the living area
EV charger, 2-car garage
Price cut from $2,119,000
concerns: Three levels on a hillside: lots of stairs if the elevator ever fails
Upper yard is terraced hillside, not a flat lawn
Seller likely to decline the loan assumption (see assumable notes)
questions: Will the seller actually consider an assumption, or only a regular sale?
Who is the loan servicer, and what's the exact balance and rate?
Elevator age and service records?
Any offers since the price cut?
Are inspection reports or disclosures available?

assumable.label: VA loan

homes.summary: The biggest home on the tour: a contemporary rebuilt in 2016 on a flat, gated 13,947 sq ft lot south of Ventura with a pool and spa. Brand new to market, so expect competition.
highlights: Rebuilt 2016: 20-ft ceilings in the living room, foyer and kitchen
Flat 0.32-acre lot, gated, mature hedges
Pool, spa and grassy lawn
Lanai Road Elementary school district
Just listed (7 days)
concerns: No loan to take over: regular financing at today's rates
Top of the budget
Valley Vista Blvd is a busy street: listen for road noise
questions: Is there an offer date?
How many showings and offers so far?
What exactly was rebuilt in 2016, and was it all permitted?
Pool equipment age?
Would the seller consider a lease?

assumable.label: Not assumable

homes.summary: Single-level 1962 home in lower Bel Air on more than half an acre, with a big great room, a Wolf and Sub-Zero kitchen and a large private backyard.
highlights: Single level, 2,531 sq ft
Over half an acre with a newly sodded lawn
Wolf and Sub-Zero kitchen with a giant island
Primary suite with fireplace, sitting area and yard access
Easy access to the Westside and Beverly Hills
concerns: No loan to take over: conventional loan at 5.85%
1962 home: ask about plumbing, electrical and sewer line
High fire zone: insurance can be expensive or hard to get
questions: Has the seller gotten a recent fire insurance quote?
When were the roof, plumbing and electrical last updated?
Sewer line inspection done?
How much of the lot is usable, and could it be expanded?
Is there flexibility on price at 29 days?

homes.summary: Renovated 1924 Spanish home in Miracle Mile with a fully permitted ADU that works as a true second home. Turnkey, with owned solar and a new 2026 HVAC system.
highlights: Main house 3 bed / 3 bath plus a permitted ADU with its own kitchen, laundry and entrance
Owned solar (not leased)
New HVAC installed 2026
Viking kitchen with walk-in pantry
Private yard with mature ficus trees
Just listed (12 days)
concerns: The VA loan is from 2026, so its rate is likely near today's rates: little savings from taking it over
Ficus trees: check roots near the foundation and sewer line
100-year-old house: ask what was updated behind the walls
questions: Has the ADU been rented, and for how much?
Is the ADU finaled with the city?
Were permits pulled for the renovation?
What's the actual rate on the VA loan?
Sewer line scope done?

homes.summary: Remodeled single-level home in the heart of El Segundo with top-rated schools, a detached rumpus room with a bar, a rooftop deck and solar. The agent confirmed a 2.23% VA loan.
highlights: Single level, fully remodeled
Detached rumpus room with bar (not in the sq ft)
Rooftop deck, hot tub, synthetic turf yard
Solar panels and EV charger
El Segundo schools (10/10 high school)
Price cut from $2,749,000
concerns: Non-veteran buyer only at a $3,000,000 price (list is $2.65M)
A $500K second loan must be paid off at sale
Smaller home at 1,963 sq ft; small garage
Near LAX: listen for flight noise
questions: Would the seller take a veteran buyer at the list price?
What's behind the $3M non-veteran price: lost VA entitlement?
Who's the servicer, and how long does approval take?
Is the solar owned or leased?
How noticeable is airport noise?

homes.summary: 2004 Spanish Mediterranean in peaceful Mission Canyon, 2 miles from downtown, with a heated saltwater pool and mountain views. The listing itself advertises a 2.25% assumable VA loan.
highlights: Listing advertises an assumable VA loan: 2.25% fixed, 25 years left
Heated saltwater pool, tropical landscaping
Cathedral ceilings with skylights, 2 fireplaces, custom tile
Mountain views, 2 miles to downtown
Price cut from $3,495,000
concerns: Assumption is for VA-qualified buyers only, per the listing
Large cash gap: about $1.73M above the loan
A $250K home equity line (2024) must be paid off
Mission Canyon is a high fire zone: check insurance
113 days on market: ask why
questions: Exact loan balance and servicer?
Would the seller consider a non-veteran buyer at any price?
Will the home equity line be paid off at closing?
What does fire insurance cost here?
Any offers since the price cut?

Main house 3 bed / 2 bath (1,559 sq ft) plus a studio ADU
ADU rent potential up to about $4,000/month per the listing
0.79 acres with a seasonal creek and mature trees
Price lowered again (down $41K, originally $1,895,000)
5 min to downtown, 7 min to the beach

Canyon setting: check fire insurance
154 days on market

Separate ADU with private entrance and kitchenette
Primary suite with beamed ceilings and private deck

Solar, generator, gym, Tesla and Rivian chargers
